independentReview.head: 391d6ccd8b8c64eaa03cce912835099790aa82e5
independentReview.reason: NOT a first-round approve, and the record should say so. The first verdict at this exact head was REQUEST CHANGES, on one blocking finding that was real and that I reproduced before acting: the pushed commit message of e5197e5b contains the sentence 'This does not fix #341.', which matches the closing-keyword pattern GitHub acts on, and issue #341 is OPEN. Merging as a merge commit would have landed that message on the default branch and silently closed #341 -- the identical mechanism that closed PR #316 two seconds after PR #338 merged, and the exact defect class this lane's own commit narrates. GitHub does not parse negation. The resolution was NOT self-certified. The tree was not edited; only the merge method changed, and that change was put back to the same reviewer to rule on rather than cleared by the writer. Its second verdict is APPROVE (squash only), and it found the thing that would have defeated a naive fix: this repository's squash_merge_commit_message is COMMIT_MESSAGES, so an un-overridden squash would have concatenated the branch commit messages into the one commit that reaches main, relocating the hazard instead of removing it. The merge therefore passes an explicit --subject and --body, which GitHub uses verbatim in place of that default, plus --match-head-commit pinned to this head. The reviewer further confirmed that squash breaks nothing that reads the record: citationVerdict already accepts a trailing (#N) as a first-class squash landing, the MERGED re-proof is merge-tree over content rather than ancestry, and the receipt-preservation guard is strengthened because a squash introduces the receipt path directly onto main. Its one non-blocking finding is ruled non-blocking BY THE REVIEWER, not by me: git rev-list --all answers from a writer's local ref cache, so a carrier ref later pruned or force-pushed could keep a stale pass alive for one writer while a fresh clone correctly reported a strand. That does not touch this receipt, whose content lands on main here, and it is recorded against #341 and #344 as a named limit on batching many receipts across a long unmerged window.
